Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using a cation effect—borrowed from electrocatalysis—to reshape the interfacial electric field and build anion-rich solvation structures in commercial electrolytes, countering negative polarization. This redirects SEI formation toward anion-derived pathways, enabling fast Li+ desolvation. Significance: graphite pouch cells reach ~88.2% charge in 6 min and stable 2000-cycle cycling, offering a practical fast-charging route.
